findings.title: --zub is never checked: a zub below Delta_n would turn the model into a non-relaxation and still yield PROVED / CERTIFIED
findings.claim: The model is a relaxation only if zub >= Delta_9, and 0.5 always satisfies that. zub is an unvalidated command-line option (heil_tri.py:102). If someone set it below the target, z <= zub < target would make Gurobi's bound drop under the target at once, and the verdict (heil_tri.py:152) would say PROVED. summarize.py never reads zub, so it would then print CERTIFIED. This is latent: no runner passes --zub today, so it cannot affect the current run.
findings.evidence: grep finds zub only at heil_tri.py:12,48,102,114. It does not appear in the verdict code (136-155), in summarize.py, in run_parts.sh or in the workflow. findings.title: Bad --split/--prefix triangles are silently ignored (not sorted, in T+/T-, or duplicated)
findings.claim: A split or prefix triangle is used only if its tuple equals a sorted itertools.combinations triple and is not in tplus/tminus, which take precedence at lines 80-82. So [3,2,4] is ignored, as is (0,1,4), which is in T+ in the boundary case. For a triangle repeated in the split, or also present in the prefix, the last bit silently wins. In every such case each part is the parent model or a superset of the intended region, so soundness is kept, but whole jobs are wasted and summarize.py still counts the split as a valid refinement.
findings.evidence: heil_tri.py:74-84: fixed = {tuple(t): ...}; then 'for t in tris' over combinations(pts,3) (sorted); 'if t in tplus: s=1 elif t in tminus: s=0 elif t in fixed'. The current n=9 split [[2,3,4],...,[2,3,8]] and the README's suggested refinements ([0,3,k],[1,2,k],[0,2,k],[1,3,k], k>=4) are all sorted and outside T+, so they take effect.
findings.recommendation: Validate --split and --prefix entries in main(): sorted, distinct indices in range, not in tplus/tminus for the case, no duplicates between split and prefix. Exit with an error otherwise.

findings.title: The docs overstate how much the certificate depends on the paper's Proposition 1; a short self-contained proof of the needed case split exists
findings.claim: The README (line 74) and summarize.py's CERTIFIED line say the certificate depends on Proposition 1 of the unrefereed arXiv:2607.15021. The only structural fact the code needs is that every optimal configuration has all three corners occupied, or has two distinct points on one side plus one on each other side (4 distinct points). An elementary affine-perturbation argument proves this (see verified_ok V6). Documenting it would take the unrefereed proposition off the critical path.
findings.evidence: check_casesplit.py output: Lemma 1 (explicit area-increasing affine map when all points on a side lie strictly on one side of its midpoint) was checked exactly on 1500 random instances. Lemma 2 gives ratio 1+4s^2 exactly. Enumerating 46656 boundary patterns, 28954 satisfy the Lemma-1 condition: 5832 are case (a), 23121 are (b) and not (a), and 1 is neither. That one is 'no corner, exactly the three side midpoints', which Lemma 2 excludes.
findings.recommendation: Add the two lemmas and the enumeration argument (or a citation that proves them) to the README's section 'What a CERTIFIED result means', and state that Proposition 1 is then not load-bearing. Optional.

verified_ok: V1 Signed area (heil_tri.py:52-61): I transcribed x,y by hand from lines 34-45, including the expression x2=1-y2, the constants y0=y1=0 and x3=0, and the vertices-case constants. Exact symbolic expansion then gives A_model == det/2 for all 84/84 triples in both cases, confirmed by 2000 random exact Fraction evaluations each (check_area.py). A is linear in (W,x,y), since w() returns a constant, a LinExpr or an auxiliary W with W==x_i*y_j. heil_tri.py was never imported or run.

V2 Orientation linearisation (heil_tri.py:84-90): with b=1 the rows are z<=e and z<=1-e; the second is slack because z<=1/2 and e<=1/2. With b=0 the rows are z<=-e and z<=1+e, slack because e>=-1/2. |e|<=area(T)=1/2 for any three points in T. Choosing b=[e>=0] makes z=min|A| feasible, and this holds for any zub>=Delta_n.

V3 Boundary T+ set (heil_tri.py:63) is geometrically forced. 2A(0,1,k)=(x1-x0)*y_k for k=2..8, which is >=0 from x0<=x1 and y>=0. 2A(0,2,3)=x0*y2 - x0*y3 - y2*y3 + y3 and 2A(1,2,3) (same with x1) are multilinear in (x_a,y2,y3), so their minimum over [0,1]^3 is at a vertex; the vertex values are all in {0,1}, so both are >=0 even without x0<=x1 or x0+x1<=1. Sampling shows (0,2,4),(0,3,4),(1,2,4),(1,3,4),(2,3,4) take both signs, so leaving them to binaries/splits is correct.
V4 Vertices case (heil_tri.py:64-73): 2A(0,1,2)=1, 2A(0,1,k)=y_k>=0, 2A(0,2,k)=-x_k<=0 (tminus), 2A(1,2,k)=1-x_k-y_k>=0 on T. All four signs are forced (exact symbolic identities in check_area.py).

V5 The symmetry reductions hold jointly. Order: an S3 affine symmetry of T moves the 2-point side to the bottom; the reflection (x,y)->(1-x-y,y) (det -1, fixes the bottom as a set, swaps hypotenuse and left, maps x->1-x on the bottom) is applied if x0+x1>1; then p0,p1 are relabelled so x0<=x1 (the sum is symmetric); free points are sorted by the final x; then the part is read off the (2,3,k) signs. Steps after the symmetry are pure relabellings, orientation reversal is harmless because the T+ signs are forced for the image, and the 32 parts cover every sign pattern of the labelled configuration. check_relax.py canonicalised 5157 random exact configurations (3188 with a corner among p0..p3) and all satisfy every transcribed model constraint at z = true min area in their part; all 32 parts were hit. 1997/1997 corner-occupied configurations pass the vertices model.

V6 The case split (a) or (b) covers every optimal configuration (Delta_9>0, and an optimum exists by compactness), independently of the paper. Lemma 1: if every point on the bottom has x<1/2 (or the bottom is empty), f=I+eps*(M,t) with M=[[1/2+eta,0],[-1,-1/2+eta]], t=(0,1/2-eta) fixes B, keeps the hypotenuse and left lines invariant, keeps bottom points at y>=0, has tr M=2*eta>0 and so det>1; by R and S3 every side's midpoint must lie in the hull of the points on that side (checked exactly, 1500 instances). Lemma 2: if the only boundary points are the three midpoints, the affine map fixing (1/2,1/2) with p->(1/2+s,0), r->(0,1/2-s) has det 1+4s^2 > 1. Exhaustive pattern enumeration: the Lemma-1 condition and not (a) imply (b) except in the Lemma-2 pattern. This covers the patterns the task named: one corner with the adjacent side having only that corner fails the Lemma-1 condition; one corner plus points past both midpoints is (b); two corners plus points past the midpoints is (b).

V7 The model is exact, not just a relaxation: every feasible point is a genuine configuration in T with z<=|A| for every triple (T+ signs are forced; a wrong split sign gives z<=-|e|). So the part optima equal the maximum min-area over structured configurations, which is <=Delta_9, and no artificial slack blocks a true certificate.

V8 Cantrell's configuration has min area exactly 43/1568 (verify_config.py). The coordinator's locate_cantrell.py, re-run, gives parts 0, 29, 30, 31 with 3 embeddings each, T+ ok and no x-ties. My independent constructive reduction lands in part 30 with no constraint violations.

V9 Fixing the (2,3,k) signs after sorting is fine. The sort only fixes labels 4..8; the split rows z<=±A(2,3,k) do not interact with the sort constraints. Ties or zero areas leave a configuration feasible in at least one part (zero area means z=0 anyway), and summarize.py requires all 2^d parts.
depends_on_paper: That heil_tri.py is literally 'model (1)' of arXiv:2607.15021 and that Proposition 1/Corollary 1 state what heil_tri.py:3-6 and README:29 say. This is attribution only and not load-bearing: the model was checked directly (V1-V4, V7).

What Proposition 1 would have to assert: every optimal n-point configuration (n>=4, Delta_n>0) either contains all three vertices of T, or has a side s with two distinct points such that each other side has a point, all four distinct. Corollary 1 would add that, up to the affine symmetries of T and the reflection (x,y)->(1-x-y,y), p0,p1 are on y=0 with x0<=x1 and x0+x1<=1, p2 is on x+y=1 and p3 on x=0. Reproduced with a transcription of heil_tri.py:13,62-90 (scratchpad/review/adv_geom/f2_signs.py, no solver). With split [[3,2,4]] and [[0,1,4]], every part has the parent's 75 binaries, and (0,1,4) stays forced at +1 by T+ (lines 80-82 take precedence over 'fixed'). With the duplicate split [[2,3,4],[2,3,4]], parts 0/1 get sign 0 and parts 2/3 get sign 1: the last bit wins. Each part is always the parent model or the model for a superset of the intended region (for contradictory prefixes the intended region is {z<=0}), so a PROVED part is still valid for the region summarize.py's covered() (lines 52-68) assigns to it. The real n=9 split and the README refinement [[0,3,4],[0,3,5],[1,2,4],[1,2,5]] (README line 55) are sorted and outside T+, and they do take effect (73 and 74 binaries respectively). Info is correct.

The mathematics is reproduced independently. Re-running check_casesplit.py gives exactly the stated numbers (46656 / 28954 / 5832 / 23121 / 1; the 'neither' pattern is the three midpoints). I also wrote a different enumeration (adv_geom/f3_casesplit.py): 18 concrete exact candidate boundary points (3 corners plus 5 open points per side at 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 3/4), all 2^18 subsets, with (b) tested by brute force for 4 distinct points. Result: 182457 satisfy the midpoint-hull condition, 32768 are (a), 149688 are (b) and not (a), and exactly one is neither: {three midpoints}. Hand proof. If every side has exactly one point, Lemma 1 forces that point to be the midpoint, which is the Lemma-2 pattern. Otherwise a side, WLOG the bottom, has 2 points, and a case check on 0, 1 or 2 occupied corners always yields distinct points on H and L. I checked the Lemma-1 map exactly as affine identities. It fixes (0,1) and keeps x=0 and x+y=1 invariant. Image x+y = s + eps(1/2-eta)(1-s) <= 1, and a bottom point gets y' = eps(1/2-eta-x). det = 1 + 2*eta*eps + eps^2(eta^2 - 1/4), which is > 1 for small eps. Lemma 2's ratio 1+4s^2 holds as a degree-2 identity. Together with compactness and Delta_9 > 0, this proves the (a)/(b) case split without the paper. The x0<=x1 and x0+x1<=1 reductions (Corollary 1) and the T+ signs are also elementary. Nothing structural therefore has to come from arXiv:2607.15021. Only the attribution 'model (1)' and the README's n<=8 history do. Minor inaccuracy in the finding: summarize.py:77 does not name Proposition 1; it says 'subject to the model assumptions in README', and the README (line 74; also line 29) names it. Documentation-only, so info.

findings.title: Tolerance inflation of the incumbent can exceed the n=9 margin, which would leave the Cantrell parts (0, 29, 30, 31) UNRESOLVED however far they are split
findings.claim: Gurobi runs with default tolerances: FeasibilityTol 1e-6, IntFeasTol 1e-5, OptimalityTol 1e-6. Within those tolerances an incumbent's objval can sit above the true minimum area of its own points by more than the absolute margin of 2.742e-6. Gurobi's ObjBound is always >= ObjVal. So in a part containing Cantrell's configuration, an incumbent with objval > tgt makes ob <= tgt impossible, and the part stays UNRESOLVED. Further splitting cannot help, because the inflation comes from the tolerances and not from the size of the region.
findings.evidence: Worst case, derived from the model rows. Each area e = 0.5*(sum of up to 6 w-terms) (lines 60-61). Each w == x*y is enforced only to 1e-6 (line 58), which gives up to 3e-6. The row z <= e allows +1e-6. The big-M rows z <= e+(1-b), z <= -e+b (lines 89-90) with b = 1-1e-5, which IntFeasTol permits, allow a further +1e-5. The IntegralityFocus doc in gurobipy/_paramdetails.py describes exactly this 'trickle flow' y <= M*b pattern. Totals: up to 1.4e-5 for triangles with a binary (5.1x the margin) and up to 4e-6 for fixed-orientation triangles (1.46x). Measured on n=7 (review/overshoot7.py, review/infl7.py, exact Fractions): objval minus the exact min area of the incumbent's own points reaches 1.203e-6 in part 5. That is above the single-row FeasibilityTol, and 9 triangle areas sit below objval at the same time. objval - 7/144 reaches +7.9e-7 (part 5), +4.9e-7 (part 6), +4.8e-7 (part 7) and +2.4e-7 (part 0). The inflation is absolute while the margin is relative (1e-4*Delta), so the n=9 margin of 2.742e-6 is only 0.564x the n=7 margin of 4.861e-6. The worst n=7 inflation equals 29% of the n=9 margin (7.9e-7) and 44% of it (1.2e-6). The incumbent only ever increases, so long n=9 runs tend to keep the most inflated near-optimal solution they find. Only points are stored in the JSON, not b, w, MaxVio or IntVio, so the IntFeasTol contribution cannot be audited from existing results. Cantrell's configuration has 13 triangles at 43/1568 (checked exactly). Whether this actually happens at n=9 is unverified: the running probe's incumbent (0.0229611, log_31.txt:97) is still far from the optimum.
findings.recommendation: These are solver-parameter changes only; the mathematics and the target stay unchanged. Set FeasibilityTol=1e-9 and IntFeasTol=1e-9, or IntegralityFocus=1, and consider NumericFocus>=1. Record m.MaxVio, m.IntVio and m.ConstrVio (attributes exist in gurobipy/_attrconst.py:373-419) and the b values in the result JSON. Calibrate on the n=8 GitHub validation: measure objval minus the known n=8 optimum in the parts that contain the optimum.

findings.title: MIPGap=5e-5 can end a Cantrell part as OPTIMAL with a bound above the target, where continuing would have reached BestBdStop
findings.claim: Gurobi declares OPTIMAL once bound <= objval*(1+MIPGap). If objval > tgt/(1+5e-5) = 0.027424840492669245, which is an overshoot above 43/1568 of more than 1.3711e-6 (half the margin), the solve can stop as OPTIMAL with ob in (tgt, objval*(1+5e-5)]. The verdict is then UNRESOLVED, although the solve might still have pushed the bound down to tgt. MIPGap plays no role in the proof logic: BestBdStop is the intended stop, and in parts with objval <= tgt/(1+5e-5) an OPTIMAL stop already implies ob <= tgt.
findings.evidence: MIPGap definition from the gurobipy/_paramdetails.py doc: gap = |zP-zD|/|zP|. Threshold computed exactly in review/thresholds.py: objval > 0.027424840492669245, overshoot > 1.3711049e-6. The n=7 analogue threshold was 2.43e-6 while the observed overshoot was <= 7.9e-7, so the sanity7 run never exercised this regime. Running the verdict block verbatim (heil_tri.py lines 137-155 exec'd in review/verdict_test.py) on 'OPTIMAL, objval 43/1568+2e-6, ob=objval*(1+5e-5)' gives UNRESOLVED.
findings.recommendation: Set MIPGap=0 (MIPGapAbs=0 too) so that only BestBdStop, tree exhaustion or the time limit end a run. The only cost is that hopeless parts (objval > tgt) run to the time limit instead of stopping early. This also removes any dependence on undocumented gap-based node pruning in Gurobi (unverified either way).

findings.title: PROVED rests on unsafe floating-point dual bounds; the n=9 margin is only about 2.7x the default tolerances, so the README's 'precise claim' is numerical, not rigorous
findings.claim: The dual bound is valid in principle. Every exactly feasible configuration is feasible for the tolerance-relaxed model. Fathoming a node whose solution is feasible within tolerance happens at the node's LP value, which is still a valid bound for that node. So the tolerances inflate incumbents (the conservative direction) but do not by themselves invalidate ObjBound. However, node LP values, cuts and presolve reductions are computed in floating point with FeasibilityTol and OptimalityTol of 1e-6 and no safe (directed-rounding) bounding. BestBdStop also fires as soon as ob <= tgt, so the reported bound usually sits just below the target: n=7 part 7 stopped with tgt - ob = 8.75e-8. What is actually established is therefore Delta <= tgt + eps_num, with eps_num unquantified. This can make CERTIFIED false only if some configuration lies within about eps_num above tgt, or if a floating-point error is much larger than typical. The README (lines 75-76) states the claim as exact ('Delta9 <= (43/1568)(1+1e-4)') and describes the margin as covering tolerances of 'about 1e-6'. For n=9 the margin is 2.742e-6 absolute.
findings.evidence: sanity7/log_5.txt:14-20 lists the non-default parameters, and FeasibilityTol, OptimalityTol and IntFeasTol are not among them, so the defaults from _paramdetails.py apply (1e-6, 1e-6, 1e-5). result_boundary_7.json: objbound 0.048615884677346656 against cutoff 0.04861597222222222. A pessimistic bound on the LP error from dual infeasibility, OptimalityTol x (136 columns + 365 presolved rows) x range 1, is about 5e-4 (worst case, not typical). The paper's standard cannot be checked (arXiv blocked).
findings.recommendation: State the result as a numerical certificate, e.g. 'Delta9 <= tgt up to solver tolerances'. Alternatively, build in a buffer without changing the claimed target: stop at a stricter internal value such as BestBdStop = 43/1568*(1+5e-5), keeping the verdict against tgt (this conflicts with F1/F2 unless the tolerances are tightened first). Or have the PROVED parts re-verified with an exact or safe-bounding solver (e.g. exact SCIP / VIPR-style certificates).

findings.title: Out-of-memory projection for 5.5 h runs: no NodefileStart or SoftMemLimit, and an OOM leaves the part with no JSON
findings.claim: In bdstop mode the open-node tree of an n=9 part grows linearly at about 1 KB per open node. A 5.5 h job extrapolates to roughly 14-16 GB, which reaches the RAM of this VM. Gurobi's out-of-memory error, or the kernel OOM killer, would end heil_tri.py before json.dump (line 156). The part then has no result file: summarize.py counts it as uncovered but does not list it among the UNRESOLVED parts. Pruning in this mode happens only against the incumbent (0.02296 since 71 s in the probe), not against tgt = 0.027426, so nodes with bounds in between stay open.
findings.evidence: Read-only samples of the running probe (pid 896). At 433 s: RSS 390,344 kB with 367,712 open nodes (log line at 430 s). At 572 s: RSS 488,184 kB with 465,316 open nodes. That is about 1.00 kB per node and 700-816 new open nodes/s. The growth is linear in the log (e.g. 60 s: 60,787; 300 s: 263,044; 420 s: 360,560). Linear extrapolation to 19,800 s gives 13.8-16.2 M nodes. `free -m` shows 16,095 MB total. NodefileStart and SoftMemLimit defaults are 1e100 (_paramdetails.py). This is a projection: the growth rate may change, and the GitHub runner RAM was not verified here.
findings.recommendation: Set NodefileStart=0.5 (the value Gurobi's docs recommend) and/or SoftMemLimit of about 12 GB. SoftMemLimit ends gracefully with status 17, and the JSON would then be written with UNRESOLVED. Optionally also set Cutoff=tgt next to BestBdStop so that nodes with bound < tgt are pruned and reduced-cost fixing uses tgt. The speedup is unverified; if adopted, check the CUTOFF-status path (F5) and re-run the n=7 sanity check.

findings.title: INFEASIBLE or CUTOFF counts as PROVED in any cutmode, although in the default bdstop mode neither can legitimately occur
findings.claim: In bdstop mode the model is always feasible: z=0 with collinear points satisfies every row. Gurobi finds this objective-0 solution before presolve. An INFEASIBLE status in bdstop mode could therefore only come from a solver or numerical failure, yet line 152 would mark the part PROVED without any bound check. The CUTOFF path reads m.ObjBound at status 6 (line 121). Whether that attribute is available after a CUTOFF is unverified; if it is not, the run crashes without a JSON (safe, but a lost proof in 'param' mode).
findings.evidence: All 9 sanity7 logs contain 'Found heuristic solution: objective -0.0000000' (e.g. log_5.txt:35). The verdict block run verbatim on status 'INFEASIBLE' with no bound returns PROVED (review/verdict_test.py).
findings.recommendation: Accept INFEASIBLE only when cutmode=='constraint' and CUTOFF only when cutmode=='param'. In bdstop mode require ob <= tgt, and treat INFEASIBLE with SolCount>0 as an error. Wrap the ObjBound/ObjVal reads in try/except so that a JSON is always written.

findings.title: The BETTER safeguard chain is brittle: summarize prints the raw unclipped points, and verify_config.py rejects real solver output
findings.claim: heil_tri.py recomputes the minimum area on clipped points (lines 143-149) but stores only the raw points. summarize.py:35 prints the raw points for the exact check. verify_config.py:22 asserts exact membership in T after limit_denominator(1e6) (line 12), so it crashes on points that are about 1e-8 outside T. limit_denominator can also move a coordinate by up to about 4e-7, which is comparable to the margin in area terms. This cannot produce a false CERTIFIED, because any BETTER already blocks CERTIFIED (summarize.py:76), and a false BETTER from round-off is impossible above about 1e-15. But the documented exact verification of a genuine counterexample can fail or misjudge it.
findings.evidence: Raw points of sanity7/result_boundary_4.json written to review/p4_raw.txt: point (0.856543815619691, 0.14345619460045622) has x+y-1 = +1.02e-8, and `python3 verify_config.py p4_raw.txt` stops with 'AssertionError: point ... is outside the triangle'. F('0.0000004').limit_denominator(10**6) returns 0 (error -4e-7); F('0.5000003') returns 500000/999999 (error 2e-7).
findings.recommendation: Store the clipped points in the JSON as exact rationals (Fraction(float) is exact) and print those. In verify_config.py, convert decimals with Fraction(str) exactly, without limit_denominator, or clip explicitly and report the change.

findings.title: Configurations that beat 43/1568 by less than the 1e-4 margin are never surfaced
findings.claim: BETTER_CONFIGURATION_FOUND compares only against tgt = 43/1568*(1+1e-4). An incumbent whose exact minimum area lies in (43/1568, tgt] would be labelled PROVED or UNRESOLVED. summarize.py does not display recomputed_min_area, so such a new record, which README line 23 promises to report, would go unnoticed.
findings.evidence: Lines 150-155 compare true_min against tgt only. summarize.py:25-26 prints objval and objbound but not recomputed_min_area.
findings.recommendation: In summarize.py, flag any recomputed_min_area > 43/1568 (or > the record value passed in) for exact checking, separately from the certification verdict.

findings.title: The SCIP fallback in default bdstop mode has no early stop at the target
findings.claim: For solver=scip only cutmode 'param' sets an objective limit. With the default cutmode 'bdstop' SCIP gets no bound-based stop and solves each part to limits/gap 1e-6, which is much more work than proving bound <= tgt. The verdict itself stays sound, because SCIP's dual bound is valid at any status.
findings.evidence: Lines 26-28: only setObjlimit(cutoff) under cutmode=='param'. Lines 127-130: objbound = getDualbound().
findings.recommendation: When solver=scip, default to cutmode 'param' (objlimit gives status 'infeasible', which maps to PROVED), or set an equivalent dual-bound stop if the installed SCIP version supports one (unverified).

verified_ok: Status codes: gurobipy 13.0.3 (_grb.py:54-72) defines 15 = USER_OBJ_LIMIT, 11 INTERRUPTED, 12 NUMERIC, 13 SUBOPTIMAL, 16 WORK_LIMIT, 17 MEM_LIMIT. All status-15 n=7 logs print 'Optimization achieved user objective limit' (e.g. log_7.txt:122). The code's label 'BOUND_REACHED' is cosmetic only, since the verdict never keys on it.

No wrong PROVED from status handling: statuses 4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 16 and 17 get objbound=None, and their names ('INF_OR_UNBD' or the number as a string) are not in ('INFEASIBLE','CUTOFF'), so the verdict is UNRESOLVED. Confirmed by running lines 137-155 verbatim in review/verdict_test.py (NUMERIC and INTERRUPTED both give UNRESOLVED). Excluding ObjBound at 7/8/10/11/16/17 only loses bounds that could not be <= tgt anyway, because BestBdStop would already have stopped the run.

A bound-based PROVED requires ob <= tgt whatever the status. A BestBdStop stop with ob even 1e-15 relative above tgt gives UNRESOLVED (tested), which is safe. All 5 n=7 status-15 runs have ob < tgt (smallest slack 8.75e-8, part 7).

BestBdStop semantics: the doc (_paramdetails.py:94-96) says stop when the bound is 'at least as good as' the value, which for a MAXIMIZE model means ObjBound <= BestBdStop. The logs agree (ob >= objval and ob <= tgt at the stop). The BestBdStop value is the same float as tgt (log: 2.7426211734693878e-02).
ObjBound is read correctly at statuses 2 and 15. JSON objbound matches the log's 'best bound' (log_7: 4.861588467735e-02 = 0.048615884677346656; log_5: 4.861190065484e-02 = 0.048611900654842194).

Tolerances do not by themselves invalidate the dual bound: exact configurations stay feasible in the tolerance-relaxed model. Nodes whose solutions are feasible within FeasibilityTol or IntFeasTol are fathomed at their LP value, which is a valid bound for that node, and ObjBound >= ObjVal always holds. So tolerance effects push incumbents up (conservative); the remaining risk is floating-point LP, cut and presolve error (F3).

A genuine better configuration found as an incumbent cannot become PROVED: ob >= objval, and BETTER is checked before PROVED (line 150). A BETTER verdict blocks CERTIFIED (summarize.py:76). Clipped points lie in T, and float area error is about 1e-15, so no false BETTER occurs beyond round-off.
The target float equals 43/1568*1.0001 to 5.2e-20. The absolute margin is 2.7423469e-6 and the MIPGap early-OPTIMAL threshold is objval > 0.027424840492669245 (review/thresholds.py).

NonConvex=2 is accepted by Gurobi 13.0.3 without warnings (grep for warn/deprecat/numer/violat over the sanity7 logs finds nothing; the logs say 'Solving non-convex MIQCP to global optimality'). The _paramdetails.py doc says the default -1 is 'almost equivalent to 2', so the setting is harmless. MIPFocus=2 (proof focus) suits bound certification. Threads=$(nproc)=4 matches 'using up to 4 threads'.
The n=7 sanity run used exactly the intended parameters in all 9 logs: BestBdStop, MIPGap 5e-05, MIPFocus 2, NonConvex 2, Threads 4, TimeLimit 360. All other tolerances were at their defaults.

The n=9 part-31 model has 165 rows, 135 columns and 50 quadratic constraints (log_31.txt:25). 50 matches the count of (i,j) pairs with non-constant x_i and y_j, i != j, in the boundary case, and the model fits the size-limited pip licence.

The model is always feasible at z=0: the heuristic objective 0 appears in all 9 n=7 logs, and by hand, collinear points on x=0 satisfy all fixed orientations in both cases. So bdstop runs always have SolCount >= 1 and points are available for the BETTER check.

verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the mechanism and checked the cited lines: default tolerances (sanity7/log_*.txt 'Non-default parameters' has no FeasibilityTol, IntFeasTol or OptimalityTol), W==x*y at heil_tri.py:58, z<=e at :84 and the big-M rows at :89-90. Re-running review/overshoot7.py and infl7.py gives the stated n=7 numbers: objval-7/144 = +7.9e-7 in part 5, objval minus the min area of its own points = 1.203e-6, and 9 triangles below objval. Cantrell has 13 triangles at 43/1568 (checked exactly). ObjBound >= ObjVal holds in all 9 sanity JSONs. New independent evidence, review/verifier/tol_lp.py: I linearised the model at the exact optimum and maximised z over the tolerance box with an LP (HiGHS, perturbations in units of 1e-6, all 12 Cantrell embeddings). Worst case for z-43/1568 with FeasibilityTol on qconstrs, rows and bounds and exact b: 3.33-3.40e-6 in parts 0, 29, 30 and 31. That exceeds the 2.742e-6 margin. With IntFeasTol trickle on the binary rows it is 1.16-1.34e-5. So the claim that the incumbent 'can exceed tgt' is correct even without IntFeasTol. Likelihood is less clear. With only the qconstr tolerance, which is how node LP vertices normally exploit it, the worst case is 2.20-2.34e-6, below the margin. The calibration in calib7.py shows the n=7 runs reached only 12-43% of the qconstr-only worst case and 8-26% of the full-FeasibilityTol worst case. F1 would need about 81% of the full worst case, or real integrality trickle. Trickle is unlikely: the LP pushes an unbranched b toward about e+1/2, and branching fixes b to exactly 0 or 1. The claim that further splitting cannot help is correct. On the recommendation: FeasibilityTol=1e-9 may make spatial branching much deeper. The worst case scales linearly, so FeasibilityTol=1e-7 plus IntegralityFocus=1 already puts it at about 3.4e-7, well inside both the margin and the F2 window. The medium severity stands: F1 blocks certification for good if it happens, but it is not shown to be likely.

MIPGap=5e-5 is at heil_tri.py:18. The MIPGap doc (_paramdetails.py:823) gives gap=|zP-zD|/|zP|, and MIPGapAbs defaults to 1e-10, which is irrelevant here. thresholds.py reproduces: an early OPTIMAL can leave ob > tgt only if objval > 0.027424840492669245, i.e. an overshoot above 1.3711e-6. verdict_test.py (lines 137-155 exec'd verbatim) returns UNRESOLVED for 'OPTIMAL, objval=43/1568+2e-6, ob=objval*(1+5e-5)'. The logic is right: if objval*(1+5e-5) > tgt, the gap test can fire while ob is still in (tgt, objval*(1+5e-5)]. If objval <= tgt/(1+5e-5), an OPTIMAL stop implies ob <= tgt. My LP (tol_lp.py) makes this the more realistic of the two inflation failures. The qconstr-only local worst case in the Cantrell parts is 2.20-2.34e-6, which lies inside F2's window (1.371e-6, 2.742e-6] and not in F1's. Reaching the window needs about 59-62% of that worst case, while n=7 runs reached at most 43% in about 10k nodes. n=9 runs explore millions of nodes and keep the maximum incumbent, so the window is reachable but not shown to be reached. The fix (MIPGap=0) is free for soundness. The note on undocumented gap-based pruning is correctly marked unverified.

The substance is right. Gurobi's bounds are computed in floating point with no safe or verified bounding. BestBdStop=tgt leaves no internal buffer: result_boundary_7.json has tgt-ob = 8.75e-8, recomputed. Gurobi's own BestBdStop doc (_paramdetails.py:95) says to 'always include a small tolerance', though that is about termination. So the certificate establishes Delta9 <= tgt + eps_num with eps_num unquantified. The 5e-4 figure is labelled a pessimistic worst case. Two overstatements: (a) the README does not state the claim as unconditionally exact. Line 75, under 'What it depends on', says 'It also depends on the numerical global optimiser. Floating-point tolerances are about 1e-6 absolute...'. So the dependence is disclosed; the remaining problem is wording and an unquantified error. (b) 'the reported bound usually sits just below the target' holds only for parts containing the optimum. The other five status-15 n=7 runs stopped with slack 3.6e-5 to 1.4e-3. No concrete mechanism is shown that could produce a false CERTIFIED. That would need a real configuration beating the record by more than 2.74e-6 and hidden by a floating-point bound error, which is the standard caveat of any floating-point B&B certificate. Whether the paper's n<=8 standard is any stronger is unverified, since arXiv is blocked. I downgraded it to low (documentation and claim scope). Exact re-verification remains a sensible optional step.

The reviewer measured about 1.05 kB earlier. Open nodes grow roughly linearly: 60,787 at 60 s, 488,089 at 600 s, 928,988 at 1200 s and 1,275,996 at 1680 s, about 714-750 per second. The GitHub runner RAM was not verified in-session.

Line 152 maps status 'INFEASIBLE' or 'CUTOFF' to PROVED without a bound check, and verdict_test.py confirms that 'INFEASIBLE' with no bound gives PROVED. In bdstop mode the model is always feasible. Take p0=p1=p3=(0,0), p2=(0,1) (y2=1) and all free points at (0,t): every area is 0, every fixed-orientation row z<=±e holds at z=0, and the big-M rows give z<=1-b and z<=b. The trivial heuristic 'objective -0.0000000' appears in all 9 sanity7 logs and at probe log_31.txt:35. With SolCount>=1 Gurobi cannot legitimately return INFEASIBLE, so the path is reachable only through a solver failure. Cutoff is set only under cutmode 'param' (line 19), so CUTOFF cannot occur in bdstop mode. Whether ObjBound can be read after a CUTOFF (line 121) is unverified, since Gurobi may not be run. This is a defensive gap, not a demonstrated false PROVED, so low is right.

Reproduced. `python3 /home/user/heil/verify_config.py review/p4_raw.txt` stops with 'AssertionError: point (Fraction(30027, 35056), Fraction(88981, 620266)) is outside the triangle'. Lines 150-155 compare recomputed_min_area only against tgt, and summarize.py:25-26 prints objval and objbound but never recomputed_min_area. An incumbent with exact min area in (43/1568, tgt] would therefore be labelled PROVED or UNRESOLVED without a flag. objval cannot stand in for it: tolerance inflation already makes objval > 7/144 in n=7 parts 0, 5, 6 and 7, so an objval above 43/1568 cannot tell a genuine record from inflation. README:23 says a better configuration would be a new record. This is a reporting gap with no soundness impact.

The verdict stays sound: objbound = getDualbound() at any non-infeasible status (line 129), and PROVED still requires ob <= tgt, so the cost is efficiency only. pyscipopt is not installed on this VM, so an equivalent SCIP dual-bound limit parameter could not be checked (unverified).

verified_ok_disputes: Item 3 ('All 5 n=7 status-15 runs have ob < tgt'): there are 6 status-15 (BOUND_REACHED) runs, not 5. They are boundary parts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 and also result_vertices_0.json (status BOUND_REACHED, objbound 0.04716993979718759), and log_vertices.txt also prints 'Optimization achieved user objective limit'. The conclusion still holds: all 6 have ob < tgt, the smallest slack being 8.75e-8 in part 7. This is a miscount, not a soundness issue.

Item 6 (tolerances do not invalidate the bound; the 'remaining risk is floating-point LP, cut and presolve error'): the conclusion is right, and it can be made sharper. My local LP (review/verifier/tol_lp.py) shows that the tolerance-relaxed model around Cantrell's configuration reaches z = 43/1568 + 3.3-3.4e-6 under FeasibilityTol alone, which is above tgt. So the tolerance-feasible region of the Cantrell parts does contain points with z > tgt. Soundness is unaffected, because such points can only raise incumbents and bounds. But it means the 'conservative' direction is not harmless for completeness (see F1 and F2), and it is not only a floating-point concern. Also, whether Gurobi prunes nodes against the incumbent with any gap tolerance (which would affect ObjBound validity near the incumbent) is undocumented and unverified, so calling FP LP, cut and presolve error the only remaining risk is not fully established.

findings.title: Corners case accepted from any single PROVED part of a split vertices run
findings.claim: vert_ok checks only case == 'vertices', verdict == 'PROVED' and prefix == '[]'. It never checks r['split']. heil_tri.py applies --split/--part in the vertices case too (lines 74-76 build `fixed` for every case). So if someone splits the corners case by hand (heil_tri.py --case vertices --split S --part k), ONE proved part k is enough for summarize.py to call the whole corners case proved, and it prints CERTIFIED. The other 2^|S|-1 regions can be UNRESOLVED or missing.
findings.evidence: Synthetic test h2 (scratchpad/review/tests.py, output in tests_out.txt) has 32 boundary parts PROVED, one vertices result with split [[3,4,5],[3,4,6]] part 2 PROVED, and part 0 UNRESOLVED. summarize printed 'Corners-occupied case proved: True' and '**CERTIFIED'. signs.py, a pure-Python copy of heil_tri.py lines 13 and 62-90, confirms the split is applied in the vertices case: part 2 fixes (3,4,5)=0 and (3,4,6)=1, with 63 binaries versus 65 unsplit. The shipped runners never pass --split for vertices (heilbronn.yml:89, run_parts.sh:18, run_heilbronn_local.ps1:32), so this needs a manual run. That manual run is the natural next step if the n=9 corners case times out, because no other refinement path exists (see C1). Realistic tree R3 in test_merge.py: raw summarize over the n=9 copy again reported 'Corners-occupied case proved: True' when the top-level vertices run was UNRESOLVED and only 1 of 4 vertices sub-parts was proved.
findings.recommendation: Do not put any vertices result with a non-empty split or prefix into the folder given to summarize.py. merge_results.py (scratchpad/review) rejects these loudly and exits with code 2. If summarize.py is ever changed, vert_ok must require json.loads(split) == [] (or run the same covered() tree keyed on case).

findings.title: zub is not checked: a run with zub <= target is PROVED without proving anything
findings.claim: summarize.py checks that all rows share n and cutoff, but not zub. heil_tri.py line 48 bounds z to [0, zub]. With zub <= cutoff the root bound is already <= cutoff, so the verdict is PROVED whatever the geometry (heil_tri.py:152). With zub only slightly above cutoff, solver tolerances make the same thing likely.
findings.evidence: Synthetic test f3: all 33 results given zub=0.01 gives '**CERTIFIED'. Mixed solver/cutmode/timelimit/threads (f4) is also accepted; that is sound because the verdict depends only on status, objbound and cutoff (heil_tri.py:150-155). No shipped script passes --zub (heilbronn.yml:61/89, run_parts.sh:18/20, ps1:32/37), so the default 0.5 from heil_tri.py:102 applies. The risk is latent: one hand-run probe with a smaller zub placed in the merged folder would certify its region without proof.
findings.recommendation: When merging, keep only results with zub == 0.5 (merge_results.py does this: hard reject, exit code 2). Never use --zub below 0.5 for certification runs.

findings.title: No supported way to refine the corners case; the printed advice sends the user to a boundary run
findings.claim: covered() only looks at case == 'boundary' (line 48), and vert_ok requires the literal prefix '[]' (line 71). A corners case refined through prefixes is never recognised. For an UNRESOLVED vertices result, summarize.py prints 'case vertices part 0: prefix = []' with the generic advice to paste it into the workflow's prefix input (README step 5). The workflow's boundary job hard-codes --case boundary (heilbronn.yml:61), and the vertices job has no split/prefix inputs (heilbronn.yml:89). Following the advice therefore does nothing for the corners case. If the n=9 corners case does not finish in one run, CERTIFIED cannot be reached except through the unsound path in S1.
findings.evidence: Test h4: vertices UNRESOLVED at top level, plus 4 vertices results whose prefixes cover all sign patterns of [[3,4,5],[3,4,6]], all PROVED, gives 'Corners-occupied case proved: False'. Test h1: a vertices result with a non-empty prefix is not accepted. Test a4 shows the printed line '- case vertices part 0: prefix = []'.
findings.recommendation: If the corners case times out on GitHub (5.5 h limit), re-run it unsplit on the VM with a longer limit: run_parts.sh <label> 9 <target> '[]' '[]' <hours> vertices. summarize.py accepts that. Splitting the corners case needs a change to summarize.py, which is outside the current rules.

findings.title: Duplicate results depend on path sort order: a later-sorting UNRESOLVED hides a PROVED
findings.claim: rs = {r['part']: r ...} keeps the LAST result for each (prefix key, split string, part), and rows come in sorted(file path) order (line 13). A PROVED result is dropped whenever an UNRESOLVED duplicate sorts after it, and the region then counts as uncovered. The effect is conservative only: the winner is always one of the actual verdicts for exactly that region, and any BETTER_CONFIGURATION_FOUND anywhere blocks CERTIFIED.
findings.evidence: c2: GitHub run-9 part 17 UNRESOLVED plus VM results/cloud/retry17 part 17 PROVED gives not certified, because 'results/cloud' sorts before 'results/run-'. c3: run-10 PROVED plus run-9 UNRESOLVED gives not certified, because 'run-10' sorts before 'run-9'. c4 has the same data as c2 but the VM folder is named 'vm_retry17', and the result is CERTIFIED: renaming a folder changes the verdict. c1 (GitHub PROVED, VM UNRESOLVED) gives CERTIFIED. Results do not depend on PYTHONHASHSEED (seeds 0-5 tested). The running probe results/cloud/probe9_p31 (job.sh: split S5, part 31, prefix [], timelimit 3600) will create exactly such a duplicate. A later long re-run under e.g. results/cloud/p31long sorts BEFORE probe9_p31 and would be hidden if the probe ends UNRESOLVED. CLOUD_SESSION_PROMPT.md steps 4-5 make such duplicates expected. The 'Unresolved parts' list also shows parts that have a PROVED duplicate (c1 output), which can trigger unneeded refinements.
findings.recommendation: Merge with de-duplication that keeps a PROVED result if one exists (merge_results.py). Alternatively, re-run an unresolved part as prefix = <printed prefix>, split = '[]' rather than with the same split and part. That gives a separate group key, and summarize.py then accepts it whatever the file order (tests r1/r2 in test_rerun_prefix.py are CERTIFIED with the folder sorting before or after). signs.py shows this model is identical to the (split S5, part k) model for all 32 k.

findings.title: Split strings are compared as raw text, so whitespace differences break a split into incomplete pieces
findings.claim: Prefixes are normalised (json.loads, sort, json.dumps at lines 50 and 53), but splits within a group are compared as raw strings (lines 56 and 58). '[[2,3,4],...]' and '[[2, 3, 4], ...]' are the same to heil_tri.py (json.loads, line 112) but count as two different splits here, and neither is complete on its own.
findings.evidence: d1: GitHub part 17 UNRESOLVED plus a VM re-run of part 17 PROVED, with the split written with spaces, gives not certified. d2: parts 0-15 with the compact split on GitHub and 16-31 with the spaced split on the VM gives not certified, although every region is PROVED. d5: a child split written with spaces is fine as long as all its sub-parts use the same spelling. This is realistic in CLOUD_SESSION_PROMPT.md step 5, where some sub-parts of one refinement run on the VM and the rest on GitHub. In test_merge.py R1, sub-parts 0-7 were on the VM and 8-15 on GitHub run-11 with a spaced split; the raw n=9 copy was not certified.
findings.recommendation: Paste the exact same split text into every run for a given prefix. Before summarising, write the split field of each copied file in one canonical form (merge_results.py does this in its copies, keeps the original in split_original, and never touches the source files).

findings.title: README step 6 can never print CERTIFIED: the results branch also holds the n=8 validation
findings.claim: README step 6 says to check out the 'results' branch and run 'python summarize.py results' over all runs. Every run, including the required n=8 validation (README step 3), is saved to the same branch as results/run-<k>-n<n> (heilbronn.yml:125). summarize.py globs recursively and then finds more than one n and cutoff, so tgt_ok is False. The same happens if results/cloud/sanity7 (n=7) is in the tree. Writing the target with fewer digits also counts as a different target: float('0.0274262117346939') != 0.027426211734693878.
findings.evidence: f5: a complete n=9 set plus results/run-1-n8 gives 'All results use the same n and target: False', not certified. f1 and f2 behave the same way. R1 (test_merge.py): raw summarize over results/ is not certified, while the merged n=9 folder is CERTIFIED. These refusals are correct in themselves; the documented procedure is what fails.
findings.recommendation: Run summarize.py only on a folder holding n=9 results with the exact target. merge_results.py builds such a folder by filtering on n, cutoff and zub, and records every exclusion in MANIFEST.tsv.

findings.title: The verdict field is trusted and never re-checked against status and objbound
findings.claim: summarize.py counts a region as covered when verdict == 'PROVED'. It does not re-check that status is INFEASIBLE or CUTOFF, or that objbound <= cutoff. A hand-edited, truncated-then-repaired or buggy result file is accepted.
findings.evidence: i1: part 5 with status TIME_LIMIT, objbound 0.03 > cutoff and verdict set to PROVED gives '**CERTIFIED'. heil_tri.py:150-155 writes consistent verdicts, so this only matters as a second line of defence.
findings.recommendation: In the merge step, reject any PROVED row where status is not INFEASIBLE or CUTOFF and objbound is None or > cutoff (merge_results.py does this).

findings.title: Degenerate splits and prefixes are sound but waste runs or are silently ignored
findings.claim: summarize.py needs all 2^d sub-parts even when some regions are empty. That happens when the split repeats a prefix triangle, which gives a sub-part with the opposite sign, or when the split contains a T+ triangle. For a repeated prefix triangle, heil_tri.py lets the split override the prefix (lines 74-76), so those extra sub-parts actually solve a region of a sibling part. That is sound but can be as hard as the sibling. heil_tri.py silently ignores triangles that are not in increasing vertex order (only combinations() tuples are looked up, lines 13 and 78), so such a split has no effect while summarize.py still expects all its parts. Sign values true/false in a prefix are never matched. Part indices >= 2^d, which heil_tri.py treats like k mod 2^d, are not counted. Results inside hidden folders are ignored by glob('**').
findings.evidence: e1 (all 4 parts PROVED) gives CERTIFIED. e1b (only the 2 parts with the consistent sign) gives not certified. e2 ([0,1,4] in the split) gives CERTIFIED; signs.py shows part 0 and part 1 build identical models. g4: prefix [[3,2,4],1] leaves 75 binaries, the same as unsplit. d4: boolean signs give not certified. j1: part 32 gives not certified. k1: a result in .cache/ gives not certified. Soundness argument: the sign-0 region of (0,1,k) is empty, since A = (x1-x0)*y_k/2 >= 0 from heil_tri.py:35-39,45. A contradictory prefix [[t,0],[t,1]] describes an empty region, so any model run on it is valid.
findings.recommendation: Before launching a refinement, check that the split has no triangle already in the prefix, none from T+, and only increasing triples with signs 0/1 (merge_results.canon_tris gives the rule).

findings.title: Results record no code or solver version, so mixed heil_tri versions go undetected
findings.claim: A result is dict(vars(args)) plus the solver fields. It has no git commit, no hash of heil_tri.py and no gurobipy version. So a result from `heil_tri.py --case vertices --split '[[3,4,5]]' --part 0` covers only half of the corners case, and summarize would still count it as the whole case and print CERTIFIED. summarize itself points operators toward this: for an UNRESOLVED vertices row it prints 'Re-run each with a deeper split ... - case vertices part 0: prefix = []'.

The open-node count grows roughly linearly, so by the 19800 s limit the solver process should be near the 16 GB RAM of a public ubuntu-latest runner and of this VM, which has no swap. Private 2-core runners have about 7 GB (unverified). An OOM kill loses the whole job: no JSON, no objbound, and no UNRESOLVED record, so summarize prints no refinement prefix for that part (see F9). This is fail-safe for soundness but can waste an entire 11 h run.

findings.claim: The part-31 bound falls about 0.005 per doubling of run time. Extrapolated (a heuristic), it would be about 0.040 at 19,800 s, against a target of 0.0274, and would need about 5 more doublings (~1e5 s) to reach the target. Deeper splits cannot get rid of the hard core. Cantrell's configuration has 4 distinct labelled embeddings, one each in parts 0, 29, 30 and 31. Each lies in exactly one leaf at every depth (no split area is zero). So at least 4 leaves must close to an absolute 2.74e-6 around an attained value of 43/1568. With all 75 orientations fixed these are continuous non-convex QCPs with 50 bilinear equalities. No run has measured how long that takes. The n=9 corners case has never been probed either.
findings.evidence: log_31.txt best bound: 0.07059 @300 s, 0.06562 @600 s, 0.06029 @1200 s, 0.05545 @2400 s, 0.05394 @3000 s. The incumbent is only 0.02490 at 3000 s, so Cantrell (0.027423) has not been found. critic/cantrell_embed.py: 4 distinct embeddings, parts {0,29,30,31} one each, no x-ties, 0 zero split areas. critic/cantrell_leaf.py writes critic/cantrell_leaf_prefix_part{0,29,30,31}.json (75 fixed signs each); a transcription of heil_tri.py's sign logic confirms 0 binaries remain.
findings.recommendation: After the timing probe ends, run one 10-20 min job with --split '[]' --prefix "$(cat scratchpad/review/critic/cantrell_leaf_prefix_part31.json)" (same cutoff). It measures the irreducible leaf cost, and through objval against 43/1568 it measures the F1/F2 incumbent inflation directly. Also run a short probe of --case vertices at n=9. Plan the refinement depth from these numbers, not from the 5.5 h wave.

findings.title: Correction: Cantrell has 4 distinct embeddings (one per part), not 3 per part
findings.claim: '3 embeddings each' counts the same labelled configuration three times, because Cantrell's point set is invariant under the affine rotation (x,y)->(1-x-y,x). It is not invariant under the reflection (x,y)->(1-x-y,y). The 4 distinct embeddings share p0=(3/28,0) and p1=(7/8,0) and differ in the choice of p2 and p3 (2 hypotenuse points × 2 left points). F1's 'all 12 embeddings' are therefore 4 distinct ones. No conclusion changes.
findings.evidence: critic/cantrell_embed.py: raw counts {0:3, 29:3, 30:3, 31:3}; distinct {0:1, 29:1, 30:1, 31:1}; C3-symmetric True; 13 triangles at exactly 43/1568; no corner occupied.
findings.recommendation: Say '4 distinct embeddings' in the reports.

findings.title: The corners model keeps a 6-fold corner-relabelling symmetry
findings.claim: Any affine symmetry g of T maps a configuration with all three corners occupied to another such configuration. After relabelling the corners to 0, 1, 2 and re-sorting the free points it is feasible in the vertices model: the V4 signs are forced for any such configuration. So each configuration appears up to 6 times. This bears on C1 (whether one unsplit corners run can finish). Symmetry breaking would be a model change and would need its own proof.

verified_ok: Cantrell's configuration (independent code, critic/cantrell_embed.py, exact Fractions): min area exactly 43/1568, reached by 13 triangles. No corner of T is occupied, so it plays no part in the corners case. It embeds in boundary parts 0, 29, 30 and 31 only, with T+ satisfied, no x-ties among free points and no zero-area split triangle.

Hand re-check of the self-contained case-split proof (V6). The Lemma-1 map I+eps*(M,t) keeps x=0 and x+y=1 invariant, sends bottom points with x < 1/2-eta to y' = eps(1/2-eta-x) >= 0, gives x'+y' = s + eps(1/2-eta)(1-s) <= 1, and has det = (1+eps(1/2+eta))(1+eps(eta-1/2)) = 1 + 2*eta*eps + eps^2(eta^2-1/4) > 1 for eps < 8*eta. Lemma 2: the linear part L with L e1 = (1,2s) and L e2 = (-2s,1) has det 1+4s^2. Interior points stay inside for small parameters because the configuration is finite.
T+ orientations (0,2,3) and (1,2,3) are forced: 2A = y3(1-y2-x0) + x0*y2 >= (1-y2)(1-x0) >= 0 whenever 1-y2-x0 < 0, and trivially >= 0 otherwise.
Refinement triangles (0,3,k) and (1,2,k), suggested in CLOUD_SESSION_PROMPT step 5, are not in T+. By formula, 2A(0,3,k) = -x0*yk - xk*y3 + x0*y3 takes both signs, so these splits take effect.

merge_results.py (reviewer tool, not in the repo) reviewed in full. It keeps the split order (json.dumps without sorting, line 79), so the part-bit mapping is preserved. It rejects vertices rows that have a split or prefix (73-75, which closes S1), a zub other than 0.5 (61, which closes S2), a PROVED verdict inconsistent with status/objbound (64-67), non-increasing or out-of-range triangles (27-29), bool or non-0/1 signs (24), and unreadable JSON (55-58). Among duplicates it keeps a PROVED row, and it keeps every BETTER row. Remaining gaps: CUTOFF is accepted in any cutmode (CC1), and nothing checks parameters or code version.

Gurobi Cutoff semantics (_paramdetails.py:378-379): CUTOFF means the optimum is worse than, i.e. strictly below, the cutoff for MAX. So CUTOFF -> PROVED is sound in cutmode 'param', where Cutoff = tgt.
Float target minus exact 43/1568*1.0001 = 5.2e-20; absolute margin 2.742347e-6.
